environmentalPersistence: High — K⁺ binds to soil cation exchange sites; Cl⁻ leaches; persists as ionic component

morphologicalEffects.heightSuppression: Mild to moderate — K⁺ is a plant nutrient so dual nature; osmotic stress at high concentrations
morphologicalEffects.wilting: Moderate — osmotic stress; less than NaCl
morphologicalEffects.chlorosis: Moderate — Cl⁻ toxicity and Mg antagonism causes interveinal chlorosis
morphologicalEffects.necrosis: Mild to moderate — Cl⁻ tip burn; less than NaCl
morphologicalEffects.newVsOldLeaves: Old leaves show Cl⁻ burn; young leaves show Mg-deficiency interveinal chlorosis (K/Mg antagonism)

physiologyEffects.chlorophyllReduction: Moderate — Mg antagonism reduces chlorophyll synthesis
physiologyEffects.stomatalConductance: Mild effect — K⁺ is actually the stomatal motor ion; complex dose-dependent effect
physiologyEffects.transpiration: Near-normal at low dose; reduced at high dose
physiologyEffects.nutrientTransport: Mildly disrupted — K⁺ excess antagonizes Mg²⁺ and Ca²⁺

microbiomeEffects.diversityReduction: Mild — less disruptive than NaCl; K⁺ is a micronutrient

visualSimulation.colorChanges: Mild wilting → interveinal chlorosis → tip burn — least dramatic of salinity group
visualSimulation.firstAffectedRegion: Leaf tips (Cl⁻) and young leaf interveinal zones (Mg deficiency)
visualSimulation.damagePattern: Mixed tip burn + interveinal chlorosis — distinguishes KCl from NaCl (pure tip/margin burn)
visualSimulation.heatmapGlow: Mild — proline and Mg-deficiency marker signature

synergies.synergyNote: Multi-salt saline soil — KCl contributes to the total ionic stress load. The educational value is contrasting KCl (dual nutrient/toxin) with NaCl (pure stressor) at equivalent salt concentrations.
synergies.antagonismNote: High K⁺ and high Mg²⁺ together create mutual antagonism — each reduces uptake of the other

educationalContext.realWorldSources: Natural saline soils, agricultural runoff in potassium-fertilized fields, ocean spray in coastal areas
educationalContext.agriculturalUse: Also used as a fertilizer (muriate of potash) — dual character as nutrient and stressor depending on dose is the key teaching point
educationalContext.humanToxicity: Very low — potassium chloride is a salt substitute for people on low-sodium diets; used in executions at very high IV doses (cardiac arrest)
educationalContext.climateLink: Saline soil expansion in semi-arid regions from changing precipitation patterns — KCl from agricultural runoff contributes to soil salinization
educationalContext.indoorOutdoor: Outdoor — agricultural; also natural coastal soils
educationalContext.whyStudentsCare: Salt substitutes used in food (Morton Salt Substitute, NuSalt) contain KCl — the same compound. The nutrient-vs-toxin dual character is an excellent illustration of dose-response principles.
educationalContext.realWorldIssue: Agricultural soil salinization, saline water irrigation, coastal agriculture

sources: Munns R, Tester M (2008). Mechanisms of salinity tolerance. Annual Review of Plant Biology, 59, 651–681.
Greenway H, Munns R (1980). Mechanisms of salt tolerance in nonhalophytes. Annual Review of Plant Physiology, 31, 149–190.
